'''Jacobus "Koos" Verhoeff''' (20 February 1927 – 19 March 2018)<ref>{{Cite web| last = Schoonen| first = Rob| title = Wiskundige en wiskunstenaar Koos Verhoeff overleden (1927-2018)| work = [[Eindhovens Dagblad]]| access-date = 2023-11-20| date = 2018-03-22| url = https://www.ed.nl/cultuur/wiskundige-en-wiskunstenaar-koos-verhoeff-overleden-1927-2018~a4b6925a/| language = nl}}</ref> was a Dutch mathematician, computer scientist, and artist. He is known for his work on error detection and correction, and on information retrieval.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.ams.org/samplings/feature-column/fcarc-verhoeff|title = Feature Column from the AMS}}</ref> He has also held exhibitions of his mathematically inspired sculptures. 

He is best known for his check-digit [[Verhoeff algorithm]], which is based on the [[dihedral group]] of order 10.

His son, [[Tom Verhoeff]], is a mathematician and computer scientist.
